Use case: illustration-story. Production animated game sprite atlas. Reference image is STYLE ONLY: retain softly shaded sculpted three-dimensional children's animal illustration, detailed natural surfaces and rich colours. It is a macaw, NOT the requested subject.
Create one friendly but anatomically recognisable Bengal TIGER, full-body side view facing LEFT. Soft sculpted fur volume, consistent black stripes, four distinct paws, white cheeks, long tail, small natural eyes. No flat paper-cut illustration and no giant cartoon eyes.
This is the FIRST HALF of a 16-frame slow four-legged WALK cycle: phases 0/16 through 7/16. EXACTLY 8 chronological full-body poses, TWO columns and FOUR rows, read left to right then top to bottom, portrait 2:3 canvas. Small equal motion increments: planted near forepaw progresses backward relative to the torso as far forepaw swings forward, bent knees pass then extend; hind legs move correspondingly, tail sways very gently. Show actual gradual limb changes, not eight clones. Fixed torso centre, fixed size, fixed ground line INSIDE every cell; all feet and tail remain entirely inside their own cell with generous 8% margins.
The SAME tiger individual, stripe pattern, body proportions, view, lighting and scale in every cell. Each character occupies most of its cell. Desired portrait 2048x3072 resolution, crisp sharp silhouettes and details. Isolated real transparent alpha, no shadows, no ground, no scenery, no coloured haze, no lettering, no labels, no cell borders. Do not add props.
